title: Classroom Practice — Speaking: Life in the New World
tier: Classroom practice; not an ACCESS tier
overview: Look at the pictures of colonists in the 1600s and life today. For each task, plan your answer, then say it aloud in full sentences. Your teacher will listen.

sections.title: Life in the New World
sections.directions: We will talk about how gathering, cooking, and eating food has changed over time. Look at the pictures, plan your answer, and say it aloud. Use the word banks to help you.

items.title: Speaking Task 1
items.skill: Describing and comparing using academic language
passage: Colonists settled in the New World in the 1600s. A model student, Rob, said: "I see a woman cooking over a fire and a garden."
Now it is your turn. What other things do you see in these pictures? Say your answer aloud.
items.adminScript: Look at the pictures of colonists in the 1600s. What things do you see in these pictures?
items.prompt: Look at the pictures of colonists in the 1600s. What things do you see in these pictures?
items.responseLabel: Planning notes (then say your answer aloud)
items.responsePlaceholder: Plan: I see ___. Long ago ___. Now ___.
items.correct: Strong answer (model): I see a man with oxen, a wooden fort, and a person cooking over a fire.
items.support: Use the word bank and full sentences. Say your answer out loud, then your teacher can listen.

picture.alt: Colonists in the 1600s. A woman cooks over a fire outside a small wooden house. A garden grows nearby and a man carries firewood.

items.title: Speaking Task 2
items.skill: Describing and comparing using academic language
passage: In the 1600s, colonists grew fruits and vegetables in gardens and got meat by hunting, fishing, or raising livestock. Now, most people buy food at a grocery store, deli, or butcher.
items.adminScript: Describe how gathering food has changed from the 1600s to now.
items.prompt: Describe how gathering food has changed from the 1600s to now.
items.responseLabel: Planning notes (then say your answer aloud)
items.responsePlaceholder: Plan: I see ___. Long ago ___. Now ___.
items.correct: Strong answer (model): In the 1600s, people grew food in gardens and hunted or fished for meat. Now, people purchase food at the grocery store, deli, or butcher.
items.support: Use the word bank and full sentences. Say your answer out loud, then your teacher can listen.

items.title: Speaking Task 3
items.skill: Describing and comparing using academic language
passage: Archaeologists study artifacts — objects found by digging where people used to live. At Jamestown they found cymbals (music), dice (games), a fishhook, and a toy horse.
items.adminScript: Look at the artifacts archaeologists found at the Jamestown colony (a fishhook and a toy horse). What do these pictures tell us about the colonists?
items.prompt: Look at the artifacts archaeologists found at the Jamestown colony (a fishhook and a toy horse). What do these pictures tell us about the colonists?
items.responseLabel: Planning notes (then say your answer aloud)
items.responsePlaceholder: Plan: I see ___. Long ago ___. Now ___.
items.correct: Strong answer (model): The fishhook tells us the colonists fished for their food. The toy horse tells us their children liked to play with toys.
items.support: Use the word bank and full sentences. Say your answer out loud, then your teacher can listen.

picture.alt: Old objects found at Jamestown: a metal fishhook, a small toy horse, a pair of cymbals, and dice.

items.title: Speaking Task 4
items.skill: Describing and comparing using academic language
passage: The artifacts include a music cymbal, game dice, a fishhook, and a toy horse.
items.adminScript: Even though these artifacts are from the 1600s, how do they show us that we are still similar to the colonists now?
items.prompt: Even though these artifacts are from the 1600s, how do they show us that we are still similar to the colonists now?
items.responseLabel: Planning notes (then say your answer aloud)
items.responsePlaceholder: Plan: I see ___. Long ago ___. Now ___.
items.correct: Strong answer (model): Even though the artifacts are from the 1600s, we are similar because we still play music, play games, fish, and play with toys.
items.support: Use the word bank and full sentences. Say your answer out loud, then your teacher can listen.
